articles.title: South Korean retail investors rebound in purchasing semiconductor leveraged products - KuCoin
articles.summary: South Korean retail investors rebound in purchasing semiconductor leveraged products  KuCoin
articles.full_text:
Huo Xing Finance reports, according to朝鲜 Business on October 25, following a sharp decline in the Korean stock market, individual investors have resumed buying single-asset leveraged products betting on rebounds in Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
Data from the Korea Exchange and Koscom ETF Check show that between October 1 and 23, individual investors net purchased 315.
4 billion KRW in 14 related products, including 226.
3 billion KRW in the seven products linked to SK Hynix and 89.
1 billion KRW in the seven linked to Samsung Electronics.
These 14 products saw net purchases of 2.
7728 trillion KRW in July; after regulatory tightening, including an increase in collateral requirements on July 31, they turned to net sales, with net outflows of 648.
4 billion KRW in August and 497.
9 billion KRW in September.
This month marks the first net inflow by individual investors since then.
During the same period, the KODEX SK Hynix Single-Asset Leveraged product recorded net purchases of 152.
9 billion KRW, ranking 11th among all ETFs listed in Korea; individual investors also net purchased 1.
0448 trillion KRW in KODEX Leveraged ETFs and 256.
4 billion KRW in KODEX Semiconductor Leveraged ETFs.
The Korean Composite Stock Price Index fell 18.
83% in October.
According to data from the Korea Securities Depository, between October 1 and 22, Korean investors net purchased $4.
8009 billion (approximately 6.
3621 trillion KRW) in U.
S.
stocks.
Of this, SOXL— a 3x leveraged ETF tracking the daily return of the U.
S.
semiconductor index— saw net purchases of $3.
54764 billion (approximately 4.
7041 trillion KRW), accounting for 73.
9% of total U.
S.
stock net purchases during the period.
The article also notes that leveraged products track daily returns at multipliers; when markets move in the opposite direction, losses are amplified two- or threefold, and repeated sharp rallies and declines can lead to negative compounding effects.
